items.extractedSnippet: What is hhw? Household hazardous waste can be any common household item Some of those half-used containers under your kitchen sink or tucked away in your garage could contain toxic chemicals that are harmful, or even deadly in certain circumstances. Some paints, cleaners, oils, batteries, and pesticides contain hazardous ingredients. Household hazardous waste, or HHW, is any chemical or product that can cause serious illness or pose an environmental or health threat if not properly stored, transported, or disposed of. Items can be purchased at home improvement stores, auto parts stores, supermarkets, yard and landscaping nurseries, and other similar places. This includes products that are corrosive or have the potential to react or combust. Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid, mineral spirits, and furniture polish, are examples of substances that contain corrosive or potentially combustible ingredients. Household hazardous waste is dangerous because Items kept in the house can spill or leak, and children or pets could get into them. Containers thrown in the trash could end up in a landfill and get into the ground or ground water. Materials poured down the drain could damage public storm water drainage systems or make their way into wastewater treatment facilities. Some ingredients when not properly stored can turn corrosive or reactive. What we accept This is a sampling of some of the most common items customers bring to the center. The program requires leaves bagged in PAPER bags only (no plastic), with branches/other materials removed first — a specific, checkable logistical detail a homeowner would need to know before relying on it instead of a hauler.

(4) VISITOR BENEFIT — still only PLAUSIBLE, not proven: this does not establish how many real visitors are unaware of LeafDrop already or that adding it would measurably help anyone, since no analytics/Search Console data is available to this agent. Residents can download a coupon to receive a free five-pack of paper leaf bags at participating Ace Hardware stores . items.extractedSnippet: What is hhw? Household hazardous waste can be any common household item Some of those half-used containers under your kitchen sink or tucked away in your garage could contain toxic chemicals that are harmful, or even deadly in certain circumstances. Some paints, cleaners, oils, batteries, and pesticides contain hazardous ingredients. Household hazardous waste, or HHW, is any chemical or product that can cause serious illness or pose an environmental or health threat if not properly stored, transported, or disposed of. Items can be purchased at home improvement stores, auto parts stores, supermarkets, yard and landscaping nurseries, and other similar places. This includes products that are corrosive or have the potential to react or combust. Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid, mineral spirits, and furniture polish, are examples of substances that contain corrosive or potentially combustible ingredients. Household hazardous waste is dangerous because Items kept in the house can spill or leak, and children or pets could get into them. Containers thrown in the trash could end up in a landfill and get into the ground or ground water. Materials poured down the drain could damage public storm water drainage systems or make their way into wastewater treatment facilities. Some ingredients when not properly stored can turn corrosive or reactive. What we accept This is a sampling of some of the most common items customers bring to the center. items.extractedSnippet: What is hhw? Household hazardous waste can be any common household item Some of those half-used containers under your kitchen sink or tucked away in your garage could contain toxic chemicals that are harmful, or even deadly in certain circumstances. Some paints, cleaners, oils, batteries, and pesticides contain hazardous ingredients. Household hazardous waste, or HHW, is any chemical or product that can cause serious illness or pose an environmental or health threat if not properly stored, transported, or disposed of. Items can be purchased at home improvement stores, auto parts stores, supermarkets, yard and landscaping nurseries, and other similar places. This includes products that are corrosive or have the potential to react or combust. Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid, mineral spirits, and furniture polish, are examples of substances that contain corrosive or potentially combustible ingredients. Household hazardous waste is dangerous because Items kept in the house can spill or leak, and children or pets could get into them. Containers thrown in the trash could end up in a landfill and get into the ground or ground water. Materials poured down the drain could damage public storm water drainage systems or make their way into wastewater treatment facilities. Some ingredients when not properly stored can turn corrosive or reactive. What we accept This is a sampling of some of the most common items customers bring to the center. If you want to be sure that we can accept your items, search it on our Accepted Items page . Here are some of the main items that we do not accept . items.extractedSnippet: What is hhw? Household hazardous waste can be any common household item Some of those half-used containers under your kitchen sink or tucked away in your garage could contain toxic chemicals that are harmful, or even deadly in certain circumstances. Some paints, cleaners, oils, batteries, and pesticides contain hazardous ingredients. Household hazardous waste, or HHW, is any chemical or product that can cause serious illness or pose an environmental or health threat if not properly stored, transported, or disposed of. Items can be purchased at home improvement stores, auto parts stores, supermarkets, yard and landscaping nurseries, and other similar places. This includes products that are corrosive or have the potential to react or combust. Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid, mineral spirits, and furniture polish, are examples of substances that contain corrosive or potentially combustible ingredients. Household hazardous waste is dangerous because Items kept in the house can spill or leak, and children or pets could get into them. Containers thrown in the trash could end up in a landfill and get into the ground or ground water. Materials poured down the drain could damage public storm water drainage systems or make their way into wastewater treatment facilities. Some ingredients when not properly stored can turn corrosive or reactive. What we accept This is a sampling of some of the most common items customers bring to the center. (3) EVERGREEN-CONTENT RISK — LeafDrop's dates/locations are set annually by the city and are NOT safe to hardcode as static page copy with no maintenance plan; if this is acted on, the published wording should describe the PROGRAM generically ("the city runs a seasonal free leaf drop-off program each fall") and link to Denver's own LeafDrop page for the current year's specific dates/locations, rather than embedding "October 5 - November 25" as evergreen text that will be wrong next year. (4) VISITOR BENEFIT — still only PLAUSIBLE, not proven: this does not establish how many real visitors are unaware of LeafDrop already or that adding it would measurably help anyone, since no analytics/Search Console data is available to this agent. Also, as before: does NOT establish search volume or ranking impact — SERP/news presence is not the same as demonstrated visitor demand.

items.extractedSnippet: LeafDrop and Pumpkin Recycling LeafDrop and Pumpkin Recycling Denver's LeafDrop program allows residents to dispose of their fall leaves in an environmentally friendly way. Each fall, Denver's Office of the City Forester partners with Denver's Department of Transportation & Infrastructure (DOTI), Denver's Office of Climate Action, Sustainability and Resiliency (CASR) and Ace Hardware to provide paper leaf bags and designated drop-off sites for Denver residents. Loose leaves and compostable leaf bags are also accepted in Denver's green compost carts. Residents can download a coupon to receive a free five-pack of paper leaf bags at participating Ace Hardware stores . items.extractedSnippet: What is hhw? Household hazardous waste can be any common household item Some of those half-used containers under your kitchen sink or tucked away in your garage could contain toxic chemicals that are harmful, or even deadly in certain circumstances. Some paints, cleaners, oils, batteries, and pesticides contain hazardous ingredients. Household hazardous waste, or HHW, is any chemical or product that can cause serious illness or pose an environmental or health threat if not properly stored, transported, or disposed of. Items can be purchased at home improvement stores, auto parts stores, supermarkets, yard and landscaping nurseries, and other similar places. This includes products that are corrosive or have the potential to react or combust. Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid, mineral spirits, and furniture polish, are examples of substances that contain corrosive or potentially combustible ingredients. Household hazardous waste is dangerous because Items kept in the house can spill or leak, and children or pets could get into them. Containers thrown in the trash could end up in a landfill and get into the ground or ground water. Materials poured down the drain could damage public storm water drainage systems or make their way into wastewater treatment facilities. Some ingredients when not properly stored can turn corrosive or reactive. What we accept This is a sampling of some of the most common items customers bring to the center. If you want to be sure that we can accept your items, search it on our Accepted Items page . Here are some of the main items that we do not accept .
